title: JANUS Engine — TOPA + Spider citation-graph expansion RUN-002
scope: Expand outward from direct artificial-gill, membrane-contactor and air-separation hits to find historical lineage, carrier mechanisms, hydrodynamic improvements, fouling constraints, cyclic adsorber heat recovery and simulation methodology.

artificial_gill_lineage.title: Underwater Breathing Device utilizing Oxygen dissolved in Water
artificial_gill_lineage.connection: Early explicit use of dissolved-water O2 partial-pressure gradients to re-oxygenate a recirculating gas/breathing stream.

artificial_gill_lineage.title: Artificial gills
artificial_gill_lineage.connection: Microporous hollow fibers harvested dissolved O2 and discharged CO2 to water; established predictive hollow-fiber design equations.

artificial_gill_lineage.title: Temperature-controlled enhancement of oxygen uptake from water using oxygen carrier solution
artificial_gill_lineage.connection: Thermo-responsive carrier creates separate cool uptake and warm release states; direct conceptual ancestor of JANUS carrier/regeneration thermal cycling.

artificial_gill_lineage.title: The photoresponse of a molybdenum porphyrin makes an artificial gill feasible
artificial_gill_lineage.connection: Reversible oxygen affinity/chemical-potential control by external stimulus demonstrates that uptake and release can be actively separated rather than relying on passive membrane diffusion alone.

artificial_gill_lineage.title: Rearrangement of hollow fibers for enhancing oxygen transfer in an artificial gill using oxygen carrier solution
artificial_gill_lineage.connection: Fiber diameter/pitch/arrangement strongly affect transfer and pumping cost; supports geometry optimization as a primary JANUS gate.

artificial_gill_lineage.title: A Fuel Cell Power Supply System Equipped with Artificial Gill Membranes for Underwater Applications
artificial_gill_lineage.connection: Closest direct prototype analog: polymer artificial gill + internal recirculating gas + PEMFC + CFD/digital twin.

membrane_module_edges.title: A study on pilot-scale degassing by polypropylene (PP) hollow fiber membrane contactors
membrane_module_edges.finding: Woven/transverse-flow packing outperformed simple parallel fiber bundles in mass transfer while retaining low-pressure-drop intent.
membrane_module_edges.janus_consequence: R0A2 should compare transverse/refresh geometries, not only maximize membrane area.

membrane_module_edges.title: Boiler feed water deoxygenation using hollow fiber membrane contactor
membrane_module_edges.finding: Water flow, vacuum level, temperature and fouling materially affect oxygen removal; air backwash was investigated as a cleaning method.
membrane_module_edges.janus_consequence: Add FOULING/CLEANING and vacuum-level curves to long-duration gill validation.

membrane_module_edges.title: Water deoxygenation using a hollow fiber membrane contactor to prevent pipe corrosion for sustainable management of district heating systems: A pilot-scale study
membrane_module_edges.finding: Pilot-scale dissolved-O2 removal confirms module performance depends on membrane area, flow, temperature and vacuum; organic fouling is a practical limit.
membrane_module_edges.janus_consequence: JANUS gill calibration must include water chemistry and time-dependent fouling rather than clean-water instantaneous flux only.

asu_aks_process_edges.title: Waste heat recovery method for the air pre-purification system of an air separation unit
asu_aks_process_edges.finding: ASU pre-purification uses cyclic adsorption, heat-blowing and cold-blowing; waste nitrogen is a regeneration stream and a three-bed configuration was investigated for waste-heat recovery.
asu_aks_process_edges.janus_consequence: Strong external precedent for a three-state/three-bed carousel whose regeneration and cooling duties are thermally integrated.

asu_aks_process_edges.title: Modular Framework for Simulation-Based Multi-objective Optimization of a Cryogenic Air Separation Unit
asu_aks_process_edges.finding: Cryogenic ASU optimization couples purification, compression, separation, heat recovery and economics through high-resolution process simulation plus Python optimization.
asu_aks_process_edges.janus_consequence: JANUS should optimize whole-system Pareto fronts rather than maximize any single metric such as O2 flux, RPM or membrane area.

asu_aks_process_edges.title: Simulation study of two units of pressure swing adsorption for producing oxygen and nitrogen simultaneously
asu_aks_process_edges.finding: O2 and N2 PSA systems were numerically cross-coupled by reusing depressurizing/purging gas between units.
asu_aks_process_edges.janus_consequence: Direct support for cross-using intermediate gas streams before venting, subject to purity and energy accounting.

spider_findings.F1: JANUS artificial-gill concept has a long technical lineage from partial-pressure-gradient devices through hollow-fiber gills, reversible carriers and modern PEMFC-coupled prototypes; novelty should therefore be claimed only at the level of the specific integrated architecture and measured performance, not dissolved-O2 extraction itself.
spider_findings.F2: The current ROTATING_AXLE_PLUS_STATIONARY_GILL_CROWN direction is strengthened: transverse-flow/structured membrane modules can improve boundary-layer renewal without spinning the entire membrane inventory.
spider_findings.F3: A new required failure gate is biofouling/organic fouling and cleanability. A high initial J_O2 that collapses over hours/days is not a viable gill.
spider_findings.F4: The three-state sorbent idea should be modeled as a schedule of thermodynamic states rather than an assumption that each physical ring must continuously rotate. External literature supports both alternating beds and physically rotary packed beds.
spider_findings.F5: Process optimization should become multi-objective: maximize net power and O2 capture while minimizing DeltaP, membrane volume, regeneration heat, vacuum/sweep power, transient complexity and fouling sensitivity.

new_measurement_vector: J_O2 versus collector pO2 or vacuum
cleaning recovery fraction after a defined cleaning cycle

Sherwood/Reynolds correlations for shell-side hollow-fiber and woven membrane contactors
oxygen-selective POMS/PDMS and facilitated-transport membrane aging/wetting data
underwater hull-integrated membrane drag and anti-fouling literature
metal-hydride H2 storage thermal integration as a possible heat-source/heat-sink coupling
ASU/AKS adsorber cycle timing, nitrogen regeneration temperature and waste-heat recovery
open-source PSA/TSA solvers suitable for direct translation into JANUS simulation code
safety_and_epistemic_boundary: All references are evidence for individual mechanisms or analog architectures. None proves JANUS net-positive operation. Oxygen-rich, hydrogen, pressure and cryogenic hardware remain later, separately gated safety domains.
